part2.question: Describe a person you know who did something difficult and was successful

segments.v: I want to talk about my uncle Tuấn. He lost his job during COVID because his company closed. He was 45 years old. Then he decided to open a bánh cuốn restaurant. It was very difficult because he didn't know how to cook and he had no experience in business. Many restaurants closed at that time. He worked very hard. He woke up at 4 am every day. At first he lost money, but he didn't give up. He improved the recipe and he sold food on delivery apps. Now he has three restaurants. I think he is successful because his food is delicious and he works very hard. He is also friendly with customers. I feel very proud of him. He is a good example for me.

fluency.band6: Accurate facts in short sentences, mostly in time order, but with no tension or reflection.
fluency.band9: Introduces the person and a hook → the crisis → others' doubts → the hard first year → three reasons for success → feelings and a lesson.

lexical.band6: lost his job, difficult, worked hard, delicious, proud.
lexical.band9: took a lot of guts, went under, at a loss, made a loss, fine-tuning, persistent, turned a crisis into an opportunity.

grammar.band6: Simple past, correct but narrow (“He woke up at 4 am every day”).
grammar.band9: Past perfect (the company he'd worked at for almost twenty years), non-defining relative on a whole clause (which turned out to be a smart move), “keep + V-ing”, and a what-clause (What I admire most is that…).

analysis.keyDifference: Band 6 gives correct facts in short sentences. Band 9 builds tension (“Everyone thought he was crazy… The first year was brutal”), explains three reasons for success, and ends with a lesson.
